seo_title: SEBI Resets FATCA/CRS Duty Under New Tax Rules
title: SEBI Moves Intermediaries' FATCA and CRS Reporting Duty to the New Income-tax Rules, 2026
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: SEBI circular directing Reporting Financial Institutions to align FATCA and CRS compliance with the Income-tax Rules, 2026
card_summary: SEBI's circular of 11 November 2026 moves intermediaries that qualify as Reporting Financial Institutions onto the automatic exchange of information regime under the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Rules 238-240 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. They must build FATCA and CRS checks into onboarding and upload certifications to KYC Registration Agencies. SEBI said the duty to report this data rests solely with each intermediary.
card_tip: A foreign investor or NRI opening a demat or trading account should expect fresh FATCA and CRS self-certification paperwork as intermediaries update onboarding systems to meet this circular.
verification_notes: The 11 November 2026 date, the circular number, the shift to Rules 238-240 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the onboarding and KRA-upload duties, and SEBI's statement that the onus lies solely with the intermediary are reported consistently across Business Today, TeamLease RegTech and CorpLawUpdates (also theweek.in and newkerala.com, not cited, to keep the source list to three). Sources differ on whether this is a wholly new duty or a restatement of a February 2024 KRA-upload requirement under the new rules; the card states only the November 2026 change. I did not open the SEBI circular PDF itself in this run, so the precise scope (limited to entities meeting the Rule 238(8) 'Reporting Financial Institution' definition, not every intermediary) rests on secondary reporting. No stated compliance deadline was found. Serves the NRI/foreign-investor audience named in the firm's current research priorities.
